mainTopic: When sprinkling the blood (זריקה) still works for parts of an offering that are gone or left the courtyard, according to רבי עקיבא, and the limits on his rule.
overview: The amud opens with רב אסי's proof that, according to רבי עקיבא, sprinkling the blood still works even when the parts of the offering are gone. His proof is a ברייתא saying a wrong intention can make an offering פיגול even about fats that were already lost or burned. The גמרא challenges him from his own teaching about אלל, as רבי זירא used it to answer a question רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן. That teaching implies that blood headed for loss counts as not there, so an intention about it does nothing. רבא solves the problem by rereading the ברייתא as talking about parts that are about to be lost or burned but still exist. Next, רב פפא limits רבי עקיבא's rule to a case where the meat left the courtyard, not the blood, and a ברייתא supports him. רבי אלעזר says רבי עקיבא's comparison case works only when both animals were slaughtered at the same time. Finally, a ברייתא tells how רבי שמעון's colleagues objected that sprinkling cannot help something פסול. רבי עקיבא begins answering with the case of a lost חטאת that was replaced and then found, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Intention counts even for lost or burned parts
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי's proof: a teaching says a wrong intention can make an offering פיגול even when it concerns fats that were already lost or burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: One can make an offering פיגול with an intention about the lost parts and the burned parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a teaching as proof for רב אסי's point. Even if the fats of the offering were lost or burned, a wrong intention about them during the sprinkling still makes the offering פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול happens when the כהן intends, during a service like sprinkling the blood, to eat or burn the offering after its proper time. This teaching says that intention works even about fats that are already gone. That means the sprinkling still counts as a real, working sprinkling even when those parts are missing.

keyTerms.meaning: One has an intention (here, a wrong intention that makes the offering פיגול)
An offering ruined by an intention to eat or burn it after its proper time
Lost
Burned

phrases.english: One has an intention regarding the lost parts
phrases.notes: This means the intention makes the offering פיגול, even though it is about fats that were already lost.

phrases.english: and regarding the burned parts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אסי's argument from before this section by bringing a source.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי עקיבא, sprinkling the blood works even when the sacrificial parts are not there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that one can make an offering פיגול with an intention about lost or burned fats.

steps.title: Explaining why the teaching is a proof
steps.stepSummary: Lost and burned parts no longer exist, yet the teaching says the intention still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: But lost and burned parts are not in the world, and even so it teaches that the intention counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the proof from the teaching it just quoted. Even though the parts are gone, the intention about them still matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An intention can only make an offering פיגול if the sprinkling is a valid, working service. Since the intention works even about missing parts, the sprinkling must count even without them. רב אסי uses this to show that sprinkling is effective for the laws of מעילה even when the parts are gone.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not in the world; they no longer exist
And even so
It teaches

steps.whatToRemember: The proof works like this: missing parts plus a working פיגול intention means the sprinkling still counts.

phrases.english: But lost and burned parts
are not in the world,
and even so it teaches that one has an intention!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָבוּד וְשָׂרוּף לָא אִיתִינּוּן בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the teaching quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Sprinkling the blood works even when the parts it serves are not there.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching's ruling that an intention about lost or burned parts still makes the offering פיגול.

steps.title: Did רב אסי really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב אסי's view by quoting a question he asked רבי יוחנן about a wrong intention for the leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב אסי really say this? But רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן: if the כהן had an intention to pour the leftover blood tomorrow, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether רב אסי really holds the view from step 2. It quotes a question he once asked רבי יוחנן, and it is setting up a proof that he was in doubt about something similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover blood (שירים) gets poured on the base of the altar after the sprinkling. רב אסי asked whether a wrong intention about this leftover blood makes the offering פיגול. The next steps show that רב אסי's own teaching implies such an intention does nothing, because the blood is headed for loss. That clashes with his claim that an intention about parts that are already gone still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב אסי really say this? (an opening that challenges his view)
He asked him (a question he was unsure about)
The blood that is poured out (the leftover blood at the base of the altar)
What is the law?

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי is the one who asked here, not the one who answered. The challenge to him comes from the reply he gets in the next steps, which is based on something he himself taught.

phrases.english: But did רב אסי say this?

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Didn't רב אסי ask רבי יוחנן:
If he intended for the blood that is poured out, for tomorrow, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reliability of רב אסי's position from steps 1-2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that sprinkling works even when the parts are missing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From רב אסי's own teaching about אלל it follows that an intention about the leftover blood, which is headed for loss, has no effect. So how could he hold that an intention about parts that are already lost or burned does work?

steps.title: רבי זירא answers using meat residue (אלל)
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא replies by pointing to a teaching about אלל: since it has no real substance, it cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: You already taught us the case of אלל! This shows that אלל, since it has no substance, does not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins answering רב אסי's question by reminding רב אסי of his own teaching about אלל, the bits of meat left on the hide. The answer is completed in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלל only joins with real meat to reach the size needed to become impure. On its own it has no real substance, so it cannot become impure. רבי זירא is beginning to build a comparison from that case to the leftover blood. Step 5 completes his point.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat residue left stuck to the hide after skinning
This shows that; evidently
Substance; something real and solid
Became impure; is able to become impure

phrases.english: רבי זירא said to him:
You already taught us the case of meat residue!
phrases.notes: He's pointing to a teaching רב אסי himself gave about the laws in חולין, where אלל joins with meat to make up the size needed for impurity.

phrases.english: This shows that this meat residue,
since it has no substance in it,
it does not become impure,
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going. The rest of רבי זירא's point comes in step 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא: כְּבָר שָׁנִיתָ לָנוּ אָלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question רב אסי asked רבי יוחנן in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זירא starts to answer by comparing the case to אלל, which has no substance and so cannot become impure on its own. Step 5 completes the answer.

steps.title: Blood that will be poured out counts as already lost
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא applies the אלל idea: leftover blood that will be poured out is headed for loss, so a wrong intention about it does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: These leftover bloods that get poured out too: since they are headed toward being lost, intention does not work on them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי זירא's answer. Just as אלל has no real substance, blood that is going to be poured away is treated as if it were already gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רב אסי himself taught the אלל rule, it follows that by his own view something headed for loss counts as not there. A wrong intention about it cannot make the offering פיגול. This completes the challenge from step 3: how can רב אסי hold that an intention about parts already lost or burned works?

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover blood that is poured out at the base of the מזבח
Being lost or destroyed
Intention, here a wrong intention that can make an offering פיגול
Does not work, has no effect

phrases.english: These [leftover bloods] that are poured out also,
since they are going toward being lost –
intention does not work on them!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי נִשְׁפָּכִין נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דִּלְאִיבּוּד אָזְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי זירא's comparison to אלל by applying it to the leftover blood. This finishes the challenge of step 3 against רב אסי's position from steps 1-2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Leftover blood is headed for loss, so it counts as not there and intention about it has no effect.

steps.title: But the teaching spoke of parts already lost and burned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if lost things cannot be affected by intention, how could the ברייתא say intention works on parts already lost or burned?
steps.simpleTranslation: But what it teaches, 'on the lost and on the burned,' is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא רב אסי used as his proof. It seems to clash with the idea that things already gone are not affected by intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1-2 used this ברייתא to show intention works on parts that no longer exist. But step 5 just said things headed for loss are treated as gone. Parts that are already lost or burned should be even more 'gone,' so the ברייתא's wording is hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: Lost
Burned
It is a difficulty

phrases.english: But that which it teaches,
'on the lost and on the burned' – is a difficulty!
phrases.notes: This is the teaching רב אסי quoted back in step 1.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָתָנֵי עַל הָאָבוּד וְעַל הַשָּׂרוּף – קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of step 5 to attack the wording of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words 'on the lost and on the burned'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If something headed for loss is treated as gone, then parts already lost or burned should surely not be affected by intention.

steps.title: Read it as about to be lost or about to be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבא corrects the ברייתא's wording: it speaks of parts that are about to be lost or burned, not parts already destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say instead, 'on what stands to be lost and on what stands to be burned.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the difficulty by changing the ברייתא's wording. It is talking about parts that still exist but are about to be destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Parts that are still physically there can be affected by intention, even though they will soon be lost or burned. Parts that are already destroyed, or an offering that fully left the courtyard, are not there, so intention does not work on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead, a signal that the wording is being adjusted
What stands to be lost, about to be lost but still present
What stands to be burned, about to be burned but still present

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'about to be lost' with 'headed for loss' in step 5. Here the point is that these parts are still physically present, so intention can still work on them.

phrases.english: Rava said: Say:
on what stands to be lost
and on what stands to be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 6 by correcting the ברייתא's text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says intention works even on parts already lost or burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means parts that are about to be lost or burned but still exist.
steps.whatToRemember: Intention can make an offering פיגול through parts that still exist, even if they will soon be destroyed. It does not work through parts that are already gone.

steps.title: Sprinkling helps only when the meat left, not the blood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits רבי עקיבא's rule: sprinkling counts for an offering that left the courtyard only if the meat left. If the blood left, sprinkling it does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבי עקיבא said sprinkling works for what left only when the meat left. But if the blood left, sprinkling does not work for what left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point about רבי עקיבא's opinion in the משנה. רב פפא explains exactly when his rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that sprinkling the blood still has its normal effect on meat that went out of the courtyard. רב פפא says this works only when the blood stayed inside. Blood that went out and was brought back cannot be sprinkled properly, so the sprinkling has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח
Works, has its usual effect (here about פיגול and מעילה)
An offering, or part of one, that left the courtyard

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Rabbi Akiva only said
that sprinkling works for what left
where the meat left,
but [if the] blood [left] –
sprinkling does not work for what left.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point limiting רבי עקיבא's ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's rule applies only when the meat left. Blood that left and was sprinkled does not have the effect of a proper sprinkling.

steps.title: A teaching supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the blood left the courtyard, sprinkling it afterward does nothing. The status of the meat regarding מעילה stays the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: If one slaughtered silently and the blood went out, even though he brought it back and sprinkled it, he did nothing. With קדשי קדשים, one is liable for מעילה. With קדשים קלים, one is not liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says what רב פפא said. Blood that left the courtyard and was later sprinkled does not count as a real sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the sprinkling does nothing, everything stays as it was before sprinkling. With קדשי קדשים, the meat is still not permitted, so מעילה still applies. With קדשים קלים, the parts burned on the מזבח never become subject to מעילה, so there is still no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: In silence, without any wrong intention
He did nothing at all, the act has no effect
Offerings of the highest holiness
Offerings of lesser holiness
One is liable for מעילה, misusing holy property

steps.whatToRemember: Blood that left the courtyard and was sprinkled counts as no sprinkling at all. Whatever מעילה status the offering had before stays the same.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
If he slaughtered in silence and the blood went out,
phrases.notes: 'In silence' means he had no wrong intention, so the only problem is that the blood left.

phrases.english: even though he went back and sprinkled it –
he did nothing at all.
With offerings of the highest holiness – one is liable for misuse of it,
with offerings of lesser holiness – one is not liable for misuse of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's statement from step 8 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that sprinkling blood which left the courtyard has no effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: blood that left and was then sprinkled does nothing, so מעילה status stays the same.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא brings a comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא backs up his view by asking what this case is similar to. The comparison he means is the lost חטאת case, spelled out below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: To what is this similar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא opening a proof by comparison. He is setting up a case that looks like ours, so we can learn from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our case is meat that left the courtyard before the blood was sprinkled. רבי עקיבא will compare it to a case where one offering is unfit, yet the sprinkling of another offering still helps it. Only the opening words are quoted here. The full comparison appears in the ברייתא in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: To what is it similar? An opening for a proof by comparison
Misusing (getting benefit from) holy property

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
To what is this comparable?
phrases.notes: He is pointing to the lost חטאת case, which you'll see in full a little further down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי עקיבא's own reasoning for his rule that sprinkling counts for meat that left the courtyard.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's rule that sprinkling counts for meat that left the courtyard
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the case of a lost חטאת that was replaced

steps.title: רבי אלעזר limits the comparison to slaughtering at the same time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says רבי עקיבא's case only works when the two animals were slaughtered at the same moment, not one after the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: When רבי עקיבא said this, it was about a case where they were slaughtered at the same time. But if one was slaughtered after the other, רבי עקיבא did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר narrows רבי עקיבא's comparison case. Sprinkling one animal's blood helps the other only if both were slaughtered together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both were slaughtered together, they are treated like one unit, so sprinkling one helps the other. If one was slaughtered first, the second became unfit right away and was never fit to eat. So the sprinkling does not help it.

keyTerms.meaning: At the same time
One after the other

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
When Rabbi Akiva said it,
it was where they were slaughtered at the same time;
phrases.notes: He means the two animals in the comparison case, the lost one and its replacement.

phrases.english: but where it was one after the other,
Rabbi Akiva did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רבי עקיבא's comparison case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling one offering's blood helps the other only if both were slaughtered at the same time.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's colleagues object: how can sprinkling help something unfit?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that an old man asked רבי שמעון whether רבי עקיבא held that sprinkling works for meat that left the courtyard. רבי שמעון said yes. His colleagues in the גליל objected: that meat is פסול, so how can sprinkling help it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught: רבי שמעון said: When I went to the village of Pani, an old man met me and asked, 'Did רבי עקיבא say that sprinkling works for what left the courtyard?' I said yes. When I told this to my colleagues in the גליל, they said: 'But it is unfit! How can sprinkling bring acceptance for something unfit?'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא tells a story that confirms רבי עקיבא's view. It then records a strong objection to it from רבי שמעון's colleagues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that left the courtyard becomes פסול. The colleagues argue that sprinkling only works for something fit, so it should do nothing for this meat. That attacks the base of רבי עקיבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the blood on the altar
Is effective, helps (here, its effect concerns the laws of מְעִילָה)
That which left the courtyard
Unfit for use as an offering
Brings acceptance, makes the offering count

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
When I went to the village of Pani,
a certain old man found me and said to me:
Did Rabbi Akiva use to say
that sprinkling is effective for that which left?
phrases.notes: He means meat that left the courtyard before the blood was sprinkled.

phrases.english: I said to him: Yes.
And when I came and presented the matter
before my colleagues in the Galil,
they said to me: But it is unfit!
How can it effect acceptance for the unfit?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלֹא פָּסוּל הוּא, הֵיאַךְ מְרַצֶּה עַל הַפָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that confirms רבי עקיבא's view and raises a challenge to it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that sprinkling works for meat that left the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Meat that left is פסול, and sprinkling cannot bring acceptance for something פסול.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא answers with the lost חטאת case
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers רבי שמעון: you agree that sprinkling affects something unfit. He starts with the case of a lost חטאת that was replaced and then found. Both animals are subject to מעילה, even after both are slaughtered and their blood sits in cups.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I left and told this to רבי עקיבא, he said to me: My son, don't you say this too? Take a person who set aside his חטאת and it got lost, so he set aside another in its place. Then the first one was found, and both are standing there. Both are subject to מעילה. If he slaughtered them and their blood is sitting in cups, both are still subject to מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins answering the colleagues' objection by laying out the lost חטאת case. This step only sets up the case and its starting rules. The real point, about what happens once one blood is sprinkled, continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one of the two animals will be brought, so the other is really extra and unfit. Even so, both are still holy and subject to מעילה, even after slaughter. רבי עקיבא is building toward showing that sprinkling one blood affects the unfit animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets aside an animal for a specific offering
Sin offering
In its place
One is liable for מְעִילָה (misusing holy property)
Cups that hold the blood before sprinkling

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מוֹעֶלֶת from step 12 with מוֹעֲלִין here. מוֹעֶלֶת means the sprinkling 'helps' or 'works.' מוֹעֲלִין means people are liable for מעילה. The words look alike but mean different things.

phrases.english: And when I left and presented the matter
before Rabbi Akiva, he said to me:
My son, do you not say so?
phrases.notes: He means: you yourself already agree that sprinkling can affect something unfit.

phrases.english: But there is one who designates his sin offering and it was lost,
and he designated another in its place,
and afterward the first was found,
and both of them are standing —
one is liable for misuse with both of them.
If he slaughtered them, and their blood is resting in cups —
one is liable for misuse with both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא begins answering the colleagues' objection from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a case the challenger already accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling can never affect anything that is פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: This continues on the next amud. The case is being built to show that sprinkling one animal's blood affects the extra, unfit animal too.
